comment: Ware tier rides the itemstack, so any ware that is genuinely PLACED as a block loses it when broken — the drop is rebuilt from scratch. Most fired ware is Unplaceable+GroundStorable and keeps its real stack in a ground-storage inventory, so it needs nothing. These are the exceptions. The block-entity behavior parks the tier in the BE tree on placement (which also makes CarryOn round-trip it, since CarryOn serialises the whole tree); the block behavior puts it back on the drop. Ingot molds already survive — BlockEntityIngotMold stores and clones the placing stack itself.

BlockGenericTypedContainer overrides both OnPickBlock and GetDrops without calling base, so a BlockBehavior can never see the storage vessel. rudiments:BlockWareStorageVessel is a thin subclass that calls base and restamps. Nothing else about the vessel changes.

The block behavior goes on the vessel too, but only for BreakageIncludesPlacedContainers — its OnPickBlock/GetDrops never run here because BlockGenericTypedContainer does not dispatch to behaviors for those two. OnBlockInteractStart it does dispatch, which is what the flag needs.
